key_findings: Portal uses standard ASP.NET_SessionId cookie. Your bot's NitrisClient already reuses it via httpx.AsyncClient.
The 2-step login (GetPassword -> LoginUser) is a server-side crypto layer — no client-side hashing. The bot mirrors this exactly in client.py:NitrisClient.login().
Session timeout is IIS default (~20 min idle). Combined with 2-hour sync interval, sessions WILL expire between syncs — see 'tier_2_session_cookie_persistence' recommendation.
GetPassword PageMethod takes plaintext password via AJAX — a portal-side security smell, but we faithfully reproduce it.
Cookies are HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax — not accessible to JS, not sent on cross-site requests. Bot must use them in httpx cookie jar.
After successful login, no further auth challenge until session expires. Sub-page requests carry the session cookie automatically.

Without the launcher visit, sub-page returns 503. The bot's existing fetch_question_papers_page_url() implements this for QP only — needs generalization to all modules.
B_launcher_then_subpage.caching_strategy: Cache the launcher visit per-session (already covered by session cookie persistence). Sub-page response cached by data TTL.

D_ajax_pagemethod.description: Direct JSON POST to PageMethod endpoint. No __VIEWSTATE, no postback. Only used for login.

attendance_failure_root_causes.summary: Attendance sync fails because of 6 layered issues. Primary root cause is the missing module-context visit (causes 503 on first GET) + hardcoded stale navigation tokens (causes 503 when NITRIS rotates them). Secondary issues include wrong semester prioritization, no session-expiry retry, and an unconditional debug-write on the hot path.

root_causes.title: No module launcher visit before ClassAttendance.aspx — direct GET returns 503
root_causes.symptom: Step 1 GET returns 302 redirect to 'Error Pages/503.aspx?aspxerrorpath=...' OR returns 200 with HTML content titled 'NITRIS - Error 503!!'
root_causes.cause: fetch_attendance() builds URL from ATTENDANCE_PAGE_PATH + ATTENDANCE_RAW_QUERY (line 105-106) and GETs it directly. It NEVER visits the module launcher Default.aspx?AppID=Mw%3d%3d-...&AppName=QXR0ZW5kYW5jZSBhbmQgTGVhdmU%3d-... which sets Session['CurrentModule']='Attendance and Leave'. Every sub-page checks this session variable on Page_Load and 503s if missing.
root_causes.fix: Add a self-healing resolver mirroring fetch_question_papers_page_url() (which already does this for QP): visit Home/Home.aspx first, find the 'View Attendance Details' link in the sidebar HTML, use that EXACT href (with current AppId/SubModId/ModId tokens). THEN visit the Attendance module launcher Default.aspx?AppID=Mw%3d%3d-... to set server-side context. THEN GET the resolved ClassAttendance.aspx URL.
root_causes.evidence_from_recon: During recon, direct GET to /nitris/Student/Attendance/ClassAttendance.aspx?AppId=Mw==-yoe1zDBzzaE=&... returned 'NITRIS - Error 503!!' page with aspxerrorpath=/nitris/Student/Attendance/ClassAttendance.aspx. Same URL navigated via the browser's sidebar (which had already loaded the launcher via Home.aspx) loaded successfully.
root_causes.impact: 100% of attendance syncs fail with 503 if hardcoded tokens are stale. Even if tokens are valid, the lack of launcher visit still causes 503 on the very first sub-page GET.

root_causes.title: Hardcoded ATTENDANCE_RAW_QUERY uses stale navigation tokens
root_causes.symptom: URL works for some users, fails for others; works for a week, then breaks for everyone without code change
root_causes.cause: ATTENDANCE_RAW_QUERY = 'AppId=Mw==-yoe1zDBzzaE=&AppName=QXR0ZW5kYW5jZSBhbmQgTGVhdmU=-eDrmHVOfXZY=&SubModId=MTI=-XTugfjokJls=&ModId=MTA=-5a3+Nygtxr8=' — the trailing '-<12 random base64 bytes>' on each parameter is a security/anti-tamper token that NITRIS rotates periodically (likely monthly or per-portal-restart). Hardcoding it = guaranteed breakage when NITRIS rotates. The SubModId=MTI= (=12) value is also wrong vs the actual sidebar SubModId for ClassAttendance.
root_causes.fix: Same as #1 — dynamically resolve the URL from Home.aspx sidebar at runtime, every sync. This is exactly what fetch_question_papers_page_url() already does for QP. Copy that pattern to attendance. Kill ATTENDANCE_RAW_QUERY entirely.
root_causes.evidence_from_recon: Sidebar link for ClassAttendance during recon had a DIFFERENT SubModId value than the hardcoded ATTENDANCE_RAW_QUERY. The token after each '-' was also different from what's in the constants file.
root_causes.impact: Random failures depending on whether NITRIS has rotated tokens since the constants were last updated. Looks like flakiness but is actually stale-token 503s.

root_causes.title: Wrong semester prioritization — picks Spring (last year) instead of Autumn (current year)
root_causes.symptom: Bot shows OLD semester attendance (e.g., Spring 2025-26 from last year) instead of CURRENT semester attendance (Autumn 2026-27)
root_causes.cause: _get_prioritized_sessions orders options as: Spring first, Autumn second, others last. Default call is fetch_attendance(semester='Spring'). For Aug 2026 (current academic year 2026-27 starting with Autumn semester), the bot picks the latest Spring (Spring 2025-26 — last year's data) instead of the current Autumn semester.
root_causes.fix: Make semester detection date-aware: if month is in [Aug-Dec, Jan], current semester is Autumn; if [Feb-Jul], current is Spring. Pass this dynamically to fetch_attendance(). Replace _get_prioritized_sessions with a date-aware prioritizer that picks the semester matching the current half of the academic year.
root_causes.evidence_from_recon: Captured Mid-Semester Seating page showed 'Academic Year/Session: 2026-27 / Autumn' as the current active context. The bot would have picked Spring 2025-26 instead.
root_causes.impact: Bot shows outdated attendance from previous semester. Student thinks they have low attendance but it's actually last semester's.

root_causes.title: SessionExpiredError bypasses retry in attendance_service — one drop kills the entire sync
root_causes.symptom: One session drop mid-workflow (e.g., between step 2 and step 3) permanently kills the sync for that cycle. SyncState.failure_count increments. Next sync cycle 2 hours later tries again from scratch.
root_causes.cause: 'except (LoginError, AttendanceParseError, SessionExpiredError): raise' — these propagate immediately without retry. If session expires between Step 2 (semester postback) and Step 3 (year postback), the entire 4-step workflow is abandoned for this cycle.
root_causes.fix: Catch SessionExpiredError specifically — re-login the client (call self.client.login() again to get fresh cookies) and restart the workflow from Step 1. Add a retry counter (max 1 re-login per sync cycle) so we don't infinite-loop if creds are actually invalid.
root_causes.impact: Single session drop = entire sync cycle wasted. With 2-hour sync interval, student loses 2+ hours of attendance data freshness. Should be a 1-2 second re-login + retry.

root_causes.title: extract_form_fields sends placeholder values for unselected dropdowns
root_causes.symptom: Step 2 POST form_state includes CTL_SEMESTER='' or '0' (placeholder) which is then overridden by form_updates. Usually harmless but can fail if server validates form_state consistency.
root_causes.cause: If no <option selected=True> exists, code uses first option's value. For '--Select--' the value is typically '0' or empty string. This is sent in form_state, then overridden in form_updates (line 106 of submit_postback: payload = {**form_state, '__EVENTTARGET': ..., **form_updates}). The override works, but the form_state still has the placeholder, which the server sees.
root_causes.fix: Filter form_state to remove keys that will be overridden by form_updates BEFORE building payload. Or: change extract_form_fields to skip dropdown values entirely (only extract hidden inputs + textareas), let form_updates provide ALL dropdown values explicitly.
root_causes.impact: Usually harmless. Manifests as intermittent failures on certain form configurations.

root_causes.title: Unconditional _save_debug_snapshot on every successful attendance fetch
root_causes.file: nitris/client.py:fetch_attendance (final block before return, around line 250)
root_causes.symptom: Every successful sync writes a ~200KB HTML file to disk — I/O on the hot path. Disk fills up over time. Bot slows down.
root_causes.cause: Code says 'Always save final snapshot unconditionally as requested for debugging' — comment indicates this was a deliberate debug request. The intent was probably 'save for debugging when debugging is enabled', but the code lacks the 'if self._debug:' guard that the OTHER step snapshots have.
root_causes.fix: Wrap the final _save_debug_snapshot call in 'if self._debug:'. Same as the step1_initial save above. One-line fix.
root_causes.impact: Disk I/O on every sync. ~200KB × N users × N syncs per day. For 100 users syncing every 2 hours = 2.4MB/hour = 58MB/day of debug HTML. Not catastrophic but pointless.

secondary_issues.title: httpx.Limits(max_keepalive=5, max_connections=10) per NitrisClient instance — too small for concurrent syncs
secondary_issues.fix: Replace with a shared global httpx.AsyncClient(http2=True, limits=httpx.Limits(max_keepalive=50, max_connections=100)). Pass per-user cookies via the cookies= kwarg on each request.

secondary_issues.title: BeautifulSoup used for HTML parsing — 5-10x slower than selectolax
secondary_issues.fix: Replace with selectolax (Cython over libxml2). Drop-in for hot-path parsers. import: from selectolax.parser import HTMLParser

secondary_issues.title: No uvloop on Linux — 2-4x coroutine scheduling speedup available for free
secondary_issues.fix: Add: if sys.platform != 'win32': import uvloop; uvloop.install()

secondary_issues.title: InMemoryUserLock is single-process only — won't scale to multiple bot workers
secondary_issues.fix: Replace with Redis SETNX with TTL: await redis.set(f'lock:user:{user_id}', '1', ex=300, nx=True)

secondary_issues.title: DB pool_pre_ping=True adds a SELECT 1 round-trip per session checkout
secondary_issues.fix: Remove pool_pre_ping=True. Use pool_recycle=600 + pool_timeout=10 instead.

tier_0_branch_year_shared_qp_cache.insight: Question papers are branch-shared: MN2101 Mid-Sem 2024-25 Autumn is the same PDF for every Mechanical 2024 student. The existing QuestionPaperCache table is already correctly branch-shared (no user_id column). What's missing: (1) kill the proactive per-user pre-cache loop in sync_user_data (workers/sync_worker.py), (2) add a branch_cache_worker that warms QPs once per (branch_prefix, join_year) tuple, (3) create a private Telegram 'QP Storage' channel, upload every unique PDF there, store file_id globally.
schema_changes: ADD TABLE branch_caches (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, branch_year_prefix VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, join_year INT NOT NULL, module_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, cache_payload JSONB NOT NULL, cache_hash VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, last_warmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW())
ADD INDEX idx_branch_module (branch_year_prefix, join_year, module_name) UNIQUE ON branch_caches
Existing question_paper_caches table is correct — no changes needed, just remove the proactive per-user loop that fills it.
tier_0_branch_year_shared_qp_cache.worker_pseudocode: branch_cache_worker: for each distinct (branch_prefix, join_year) in users table: pick any one student from this branch, login as them, iterate all years in YEAR_MAP × all subjects in their attendance, for each (subject, year, exam_type) not in QuestionPaperCache: sync metadata + download PDF + upload to Telegram 'QP Storage' channel + store telegram_file_id

tier_1_per_module_ttl_sync.insight: Replace the single SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS=7200 with per-module TTLs based on data volatility. The current 'sync everything every 2 hours' is wrong because attendance updates daily but timetable changes only at semester boundary.

ttl_table.seating_chart: 1 hour during exam season, 1 day otherwise
ttl_table.grade_card: 1 day after result declaration, else 7 days

schema_changes: ADD TABLE module_sync_schedule (user_id BIGINT, module_name VARCHAR(100), last_synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ, next_sync_at TIMESTAMPTZ, last_status VARCHAR(20), last_error TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (user_id, module_name))

tier_2_session_cookie_persistence.insight: After successful login, persist ASP.NET_SessionId + any auth cookies encrypted in DB. Most sync cycles skip the 3-request login flow entirely. Combined with per-module TTLs, requests/user/sync go from ~10 to ~2.
schema_changes: ADD COLUMN users.session_cookies_json JSONB (encrypted with same Fernet key as encrypted_password)
tier_2_session_cookie_persistence.flow_pseudocode: sync_user_data: load user.session_cookies_json (if exists + not expired) -> set on httpx client -> try first request -> if 302 to Login.aspx -> fall back to full re-login -> update session_cookies_json

tier_3_first_student_of_branch_warming.insight: For branch-shared data (QP, exam schedule, seating chart per branch per year), the first student of any (branch, year) tuple warms the cache; subsequent students hit the cache -> 0 portal requests for branch-shared data.
tier_3_first_student_of_branch_warming.implementation_notes: When student A from 725MN (Mech 2025) syncs for the first time, branch_cache_worker warms the (725MN, 2025) cache row. When students B, C, D from same branch sync later, they hit the cache row — their personal sync only fetches user-specific data (their own attendance, their inbox, their own grade card).

tier_4_webmail_integration.insight: Home.aspx leaks webmail + MS Teams passwords in plaintext. Bot can scrape these once per session, then IMAP-fetch student email from nitrkl.ac.in webmail. Pushes new-email notifications to Telegram. Catches notices profs send via email but never post on NITRIS messages.
schema_changes: ADD TABLE webmail_credentials (user_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, email VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL, encrypted_password VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL, webmail_provider VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'gmail', last_synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ, last_seen_uid BIGINT)

ADD TABLE email_messages (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id BIGINT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, uid BIGINT NOT NULL, sender VARCHAR(200), subject VARCHAR(500), body TEXT, received_at TIMESTAMPTZ, telegram_notification_sent BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, UNIQUE(user_id, uid))
tier_4_webmail_integration.implementation_notes: Confirm nitrkl.ac.in uses Google Workspace (Home.aspx links https://gmail.com — strongly suggests yes). If yes, IMAP via imap.gmail.com:993 with app-password (or OAuth). If no, find the actual mail server via DNS MX lookup: dig MX nitrkl.ac.in
